tables: STANDARD 23: PROVISION OF AND CONTINUITY OF CARE (MANDATORY STANDARD)

STANDARD: The Healthcare Organisation ensures patients are provided with safe, high- quality inpatient and outpatient care throughout the care delivery process. They should do this from the time that the patient enters the healthcare organisation or service through to when the patient is discharged or transferred to another health facility-service; and during any ongoing care they provide after discharge.
The Healthcare Organisation should implement evidence-based practice and a have a process for assessing the appropriateness and effectiveness of care and services, and the settings they are delivered in.
Source(s)
Standard 17 National Health Service Standards (NHSS) Vol. 2 (2nd Edition) National Quality Standard

ORGANISATION AND MANAGEMENT

The Otorhinolaryngology Services shall be organised, directed and coordinated with other services in the facility to provide a standard of inpatient and outpatient care to the community in a safe, effective, efficient and caring manner. The Otorhinolaryngology services should be accessible, and continuity of care assured.

The Vision, Mission of the Facility are accessible. The Goals of the Otorhinolaryngology Services suit its scope and are clearly documented. It should reflect the aspirations of the service and the needs of the community.
Evidence of Compliance
The Mission, Vision and Goals of the Organisation are visible, endorsed and dated.
There is an endorsed and dated department Organisational chart with lines of functions and reporting relationships.
Relevant policies are available in the department. (National Health Plan, National Health Service Standards, etc.).
Evidence of submission of an Annual Implementation Plan and budget.
Evidence of fee structure (if fees are collected).

There is a mechanism to ensure effective interaction between the Head of the Services and the Organisation’s Governing Body and Senior Management. The Head of Services shall also be involved for the following aspects of 
management of the services;
Preparation of budget and ensuring that expenditure remains within the budget allocated
Human resource
Facility and equipment management
Safety and performance improvement activities and risk management
Evidence of Compliance
Letter of appointment and terms of reference as the Head of Service
Letter of appointment and terms of reference in other hospital committees.
Evidence of (a) to (d) in meeting minutes/correspondence of the Otorhinolaryngology Services indicating the involvement of the Head of Service.
Request for allocation for budget and staffing.

Regular staff meetings are held between Head of Service and staff with sufficient regularity to discuss issues pertaining to the Otorhinolaryngology Services. These meetings are minuted and communicated to all staff.
Evidence of Compliance
Meeting minutes are available, disseminated and acknowledged by staff.
There is sufficient attendance for the meetings with adequate representatives of the service.
Frequency of meetings are as scheduled.
Discussions and resolutions are implemented (problems not solved are brought forward to the next meeting till resolved).

Appropriate statistics and records are maintained in the department in and used for managing services and patient care.
The following (among others) are available;
Workload/census for inpatients and outpatients
Quarterly and annual report
Incident reports and register
Staffing number and staff profile
Staff training records
Data on performance improvement
Number of referrals to the Otorhinolaryngology Services
Evidence of Compliance
The statistics and records from (a) to (f) are available.
The NHSS Toolkit Assessment (checklist) for the relevant level has been completed in the past 6 months.
HUMAN RESOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT

The Otorhinolaryngology Services shall be directed by a qualified and competent medical practitioner, and staffed by suitably qualified and competent clinical staff to achieve the goals and objectives of the Otorhinolaryngology Services. There are sufficient staffing levels, a staff supervision structure, performance appraisals and ongoing commitment to continuing medical education.

The are written and dated job descriptions for each category of staff that include:
Qualification, training and experience for the position
Lines of authority
Accountability, functions and responsibilities
Reviewed when required if there is major change in job scope 
Statutory regulations
Administrative and clinical job scope
Evidence of Compliance
There are dated and specific job descriptions for each staff that include (a) to (f).
The job description is acknowledged by the staff and signed by the Head of Service and dated.
The scope of work in the job description aligns with the training, skill and experience of the staff (credentialling)
The staff holds current registration with the relevant professional body.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of current registration for all cadres of staff (annual practicing certificate).
The staff works within their job description and job scope.
Evidence of Compliance
Observation that cadres of staff are working according to their job description and job scope.
There are continuing education activities for staff to pursue professional interests and to prepare for current and future changes in practice.
Evidence of Compliance
Training calendar includes in-house/ external courses/ workshops/ conferences.
Training for each staff including training in life support is kept in the Department.
There are ongoing Continuous Professional Activities in the Department.
The educational needs of staff are addressed following findings from incidents reports, mortality audits and performance improvement studies.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of staff training because of recommendations made from incident reports or mortality and morbidity reviews.

In a Facility where undergraduate medical, nursing and allied health training programmes are conducted, the Facility shall ensure there are sufficient skilled trained staff to provide clinical supervision of students.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of sufficient skilled trained staff to provide clinical supervision as per terms of Memorandum of Understanding.
Staff, including medical practitioners, receive evaluation of their performance at the completion of the probationary period and annually thereafter, or as defined by the Organisation.
Evidence of Compliance
Performance appraisal for staff, including medical practitioners, is completed upon probationary period and as an annual exercise.
Where appropriate the Facility shall endeavour to undertake clinical research using available resources.
Evidence of Compliance
Documented evidence of research activities in the Department.

Staffing levels are based on the following;
The number of persons deployed is proportional to the number of patients being cared for as per regulatory requirements and for the intensity of care provided
The categories of service providers reflect the complexity of clinical problems being managed
Staffing needs shall take into consideration absences due to leave or illness; double shift duties by clinical staff shall be documented and monitored
Adequate staffing levels of appropriate competency shall be maintained throughout the hours the services are in operation. 
Where it is not possible to have service providers on duty on site, e.g. after working hours, provision is made for relevant medical practitioner to be available on call.
Evidence of Compliance

Planning of staff allocation and movement within the Department includes the following;
Deployment based on staff to patient ratio, bed occupancy rate and complexity of cases.
Special skills/training of staff.
Contingency plan for acute shortage.
Duty roster.
Evidence that all clinicians re not made to work more than the stipulated hours.

There is a structured orientation programme for all newly appointed staff to the Psychiatry Services including medical practitioners and for those new to specific areas that include the following;
Explanation of the goals, objectives, policies and procedures of the Facility and those of the Psychiatry Services
Lines of authority and areas of responsibility 
Explanation of duties and functions
Explanation of the methods of assigning clinical care and the standards of clinical practice 
Handover communication
Processes for resolving practice/ethical dilemmas in a timely manner
Information about safety procedures 
Training in basic/advanced life support techniques
Methods of obtaining appropriate resource materials
Staff appraisal procedures for the Otorhinolaryngology Services
Education on Patient and Family Rights
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of policy stating that all staff have to attend a structured orientation programme.
Attendance list of those having attended the orientation programme.
POLICIES AND PROCEDURES

There are written and dated policies for all activities of the Otorhinolaryngology Services. These policies reflect current standards of medical practice, relevant regulations and statutory requirements. These policies and procedures, terms of reference, by laws, rules and regulations state how the clinical staff regulate themselves and provide patient care.
There are written policies and procedures for the Otorhinolaryngology Services which are consistent with the overall policies of the Facility, regulatory requirements and current standard practices.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of documented policies and procedures for the service.
The policies and procedures are endorsed and dated.
There is a periodic review at least once in three years.
Copies of policies, by laws, regulations and relevant acts are accessible on site for staff reference.
Policies and procedures are developed by a committee in collaboration with staff and with other departments if needed.
Evidence of Compliance
Minutes of committee meetings on development and revision on policies and procedures.

The policies and procedures documentation shall address at least the following topics;
Description of the organisational structure of the Otorhinolaryngology Services
The use of updated Standard Treatment Guidelines.
Handover communication
Drug prescription, dispensing and administration
Blood transfusion 
Continuing of care including regular review of patient and review of investigation results
Admission and Discharge (planned or “At Own Risk”)
Referrals and Repatriations
Guardians for patients
Management of cases with an infectious disease including notification of notifiable diseases
Internal and External Disaster
Incident reports 
Management of deaths. 
Health information system and Medical Records.
Outreach and supervisory visits including school visits.
Infection Prevention and Control
Management of acutely deteriorating patients.
Patient feedback and complaint mechanism.
Informed consent
Evidence of Compliance
Documented policies and procedures that address (a) to (s).
Staff are briefed on the policies and procedures (meeting minutes or circulation acknowledgement).
The service shall operate on a 24-hour basis providing level of care appropriate the facility.
Evidence of Compliance
Operational policy on 24-hour service.
Staffing level reflects a good mix of senior and junior staff.
On call roster is dated and authorised.
The service shall ensure that provision of patient care and services achieve effective outcomes and is safe.
Evidence of Compliance
Relevant updated Standard Treatment Guidelines are available in the division.
Patient register is updated daily.
Evidence of appropriate admission process.
Evidence of in-patient and guardian orientation process during admission.
Evidence of initial assessment and provisional diagnosis.
Evidence and documentation of morning and evening rounds.
Evidence of regular vital sign documentation.
Documentation of discussions with patient/family/guardian about the patient’s condition.
Evidence of discussions with other disciplines and referrals if necessary.
Evidence of patient handover during shift change (documentation and observed).
Evidence of documented informed consent for procedures.
Evidence of flowchart on patient deterioration or “Code Blue” procedures.
Discharge summaries are issued to patients on discharge with a care plan.
Evidence of a patient referral register.

There is a standardised patient medical record.
This record should have the following:
An identification page with patient’s weight and immunisation status.
Vital sign monitoring sheet (BP, HR, SpO2, Conscious level) 
Patient history
Clinical notes
Consent form
Diagnostic reports
Final diagnosis and code at time of discharge
Drug order/medication sheet
Operating theatre sheet (if appropriate)
Allergy and adverse reaction documentation
Behaviour issues that may pose a risk.
Discharge summary
Referral form (if applicable)
Evidence of Compliance
Patient’s medical record has elements (a) to (m).
The Patient’s medical record has a unique identifier (MRN).
Evidence of clinical documentation which is signed, dated and with legible writing.
Evidence of use of appropriate abbreviations.
FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT

The Head of Otorhinolaryngology Services shall ensure adequate facilities and equipment that are safe and appropriate are available for the staff to function effectively and to meet the goals and objectives of the Otorhinolaryngology Services.
There are adequate and appropriate facilities and equipment with proper utilisation of space to enable staff to carry out their professional, teaching and administrative functions.
Evidence of Compliance
The building is sound and there is adequate space to match the services.
Appropriate type of equipment to match the complexity of services.
Adequate facilities and equipment at each patient care area for safe care. (e.g. defibrillators, emergency trolley, hand washing facilities etc).
Easy access and clear (unblocked) exit routes.
Absence of overcrowding.
Availability of an isolation area.
There are lights/lamps/solar for blackouts.
There is good ventilation within the ward/s.
There is running water in the facility
Waste is segregated at the facility at the point of generation.
Existing facilities shall consider the safety and comfort of staff and patients.
Evidence of Compliance
Design and layout of the unit, e.g. wards, treatment rooms, dirty and clean utility rooms, access, lighting, signage, etc. address the safety aspects of patients and staff.
Equipment should have scheduled planned preventive maintenance (PPM).
There is access to hand washing facilities.
Mattresses are covered with waterproof coverings and there is clean linen on every bed.
Sharps are disposed properly.
There is a designated area in the ward for ill patients who require extra supervision.
Suitable forms of communication systems and equipment are provided to enable clinical staff to communicate among themselves and with the other members of the healthcare team.
Evidence of Compliance
Appropriate telecommunication modalities available for daily operation and during emergencies.
There is optimal management of beds at the Department with documentation of total number of beds and monitoring of bed occupancy rates.
Evidence of Compliance
There is up-to-date documentation of the total number of beds (overnight and day-only beds).
Evidence that any patient who occupies a bed for more than 4 hours and receives significant clinical care is classified as an “in-patient”.
Factors such as “bed occupancy rates” and “average length of stay” are monitored and analysed.
Facilities are suitably located to facilitate easy access and to provide an atmosphere of user, environmental and ‘disabled' friendly
Evidence of Compliance
Floor plan indicates accessibility and patient and user friendly.
Feedback from patient satisfaction survey.
Incident reporting relating to facilities if any.
Toilets have wheelchair access.
Equipment, both for emergency and non-emergency usage, shall be appropriate to the level of care.
Evidence of Compliance

Availability of emergency and non-emergency equipment appropriate to level of care, such as defibrillator, emergency trolley, suction machine, electrocardiogram (ECG) machine, infusion or syringe pump, vital sign monitor, pulse oximeter, oxygen concentrator etc.
Scheduled checking of items in emergency trolley.
There are adequate patient transfer trolleys, wheelchairs, mobility aids and a dedicated drug fridge.
There is a dedicated cabinet for dangerous drugs which can be locked.

There is evidence that the facility has a comprehensive maintenance programme such as predictive maintenance, planned preventive maintenance and calibration activities, to ensure the facilities and equipment are in good working order.
Evidence of Compliance
Planned Preventive Maintenance records such as schedule, stickers, etc.
Planned Replacement Programme where applicable.
Complaint records.
Asset inventory.
Where specialised equipment is used, there is evidence that only staff who are trained and authorised by the Facility operate such equipment.
Evidence of Compliance
User training records.
List of staff trained and authorised to operate specialised equipment.

The Specialist Outpatient Services shall have the following features;
The organisation and management of the clinics are planned to ensure minimal waiting time, and avoidance of unnecessary visits by the patients
Record keeping shall be efficient
An appointment or queuing system is used to manage patient consultations
The clinic is easily accessible including for non-ambulant patients and is easily identified through adequate signage
The clinic is located close to other facilities, e.g. radiology, laboratories and pharmacy
Adequate provision is made for patient comfort
Call back system (especially for high- risk cases)
Avenue for patients to access service between appointments
Monitoring of data
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of list of services available and offered to patients.
Flow chart on work process.
Safe keeping of medical records.
Clinic appointment system.
Security of data in Health Information System.
Monitoring of waiting time.
Adequate and appropriate signage.
Floor plan indicates accessibility to supporting services and optimisation of space.
Adequate patient personal use items, e.g. wheelchair, mobility aids etc.
Adequate waiting area, toilets and reading material.
Evidence of data collected as per point (i).

At the Outpatient Clinic, adequate numbers of rooms are provided to ensure patient privacy and confidentiality for various patient care activities including:
Consultation (not more than one patient in a room at any time). 
Minor procedures and nursing procedures. 
Performance of various tests.
Evidence of Compliance
Evidence of facilities with patient privacy ensured.
Procedure room appropriately equipped.
Patient monitoring device is available where required (vital signs).
List of procedures performed.
The following equipment are available (slit lamp bio microscope, ophthalmoscopes).
SAFETY AND PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT ACTIVITIES

The Head of Otorhinolaryngology Services shall ensure the provision of quality performance with staff involvement in the continuous safety and performance improvement activities of the Otorhinolaryngology Services.
There are planned activities for performance and quality improvement.
Evidence of Compliance
There is a designated person who monitors safety and performance improvement activities within the Psychiatry Services.
There are records/registers on performance improvement activities.
There are meeting minutes for performance improvement meetings.
There are records on innovation (if any)

The Head of Otorhinolaryngology Services shall ensure that the staff are trained and complete incident reports which are promptly reported, investigated, discussed by the staff and forwarded to the Officer in Charge (OIC) of the Facility. Selected incidents have Root Cause Analysis (RCA) done in an agreed time frame to prevent recurrence.
Evidence of Compliance

System for incident reporting is in place with the following;
Training of staff in incident reporting
Policy on incident reporting
Method/SOP on Incident reporting
Register of incidents
Completed incident reports.
Corrective and preventive action plans.
Minutes of meeting.
Involved staff given feedback about the incident report.
Acknowledgment by Head of Otorhinolaryngology Service and Director of Curative Services.

Specific performance indicators are tracked for e.g.;
Something to go here??
Evidence of Compliance
Specific performance indicators are monitored.
Remedial action is taken when appropriate.
